test_title: PYST 8: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Globalisation influenced consumer choices in India. Which trend reflects the impact of globalisation on Indian consumers?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Wider availability of international brands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Globalisation** refers to the increasing interconnectedness of economies, cultures, and societies, which has significantly influenced consumer choices in India.
 
• One prominent impact of globalisation is the **wider availability of international brands** in the Indian market, giving consumers access to a diverse range of products from across the globe.
 
• Foreign brands such as **Nike, Adidas, Apple, Samsung, McDonald's, and Starbucks** have established a strong presence in India, catering to the demand for globally recognized products.
 
• Indian consumers now have exposure to **global trends, innovations, and quality standards**, which have shaped their preferences and expectations.
 
• The opening up of the Indian economy in **1991** through economic reforms and liberalization facilitated the entry of international brands into the market.
 
• This trend has led to the **diversification of consumer options**, allowing individuals to choose products and services that align with their preferences and aspirations.
 
• Globalisation has also influenced the **lifestyle, fashion choices, and consumption patterns** of Indian consumers, making them more cosmopolitan.
 
• The Indian government’s policies, such as **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in retail, have further boosted the presence of international brands in India.
 
• Overall, globalisation has expanded the scope of consumer choices, enabling individuals in India to access products that were once unavailable or limited to certain regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Decline in foreign goods**__

 __
 
• This is not correct because globalisation has resulted in an **increase** rather than a decline in the availability and consumption of foreign goods in India.
 
• Foreign goods have gained popularity due to **higher quality, better branding, and aspirational value**.
 
• Brands like **Coca-Cola, Nestlé, and Unilever** have seen substantial growth in India due to globalisation.
 
 
 
• **Less brand diversity**__
 __
 
• Globalisation has actually led to **greater brand diversity**, providing Indian consumers with a broader range of choices.
 
• From luxury brands like **Gucci and Louis Vuitton** to affordable options like **H&M and Zara**, consumers have access to diverse categories of products.
 
 
 
• **Monopolisation of FMCG**__
 
 
• While globalisation has increased competition, it has not led to monopolisation in the **Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG)** sector.
 
• Instead, multiple brands, both local and international, coexist, offering consumers varied choices in this segment.
 
• Brands such as **Colgate, Britannia, Dabur**, and **Procter & Gamble** compete in this diversified market.
